item.title: A Chinese A.I. Lab May Test the World’s Cybersecurity With a Model
item.description: In July, an unreleased OpenAI model went rogue and demonstrated remarkable hacking abilities. This week, a lab called Z.ai will release a similarly powerful system to everyone.
item.dc:creator: Cade Metz
item.media:description: A Chinese lab called Z.ai is preparing to release similar A.I. technology as “open weight” software.

item.title: Anatomy of an Autonomous Attack: 5 Alarming A.I. Capabilities
item.description: When OpenAI’s agents went rogue in July, they demonstrated ingenuity and drive beyond what many experts imagined — a dangerous harbinger of what such bots could do in the future.
item.dc:creator: Dylan Freedman
item.media:credit: The New York Times; source photos by Aaron Wojack and Ulysses Ortega for The New York Times

item.title: Wildfires Are Turning Forests in the American West Into Shrubland
item.description: Towering woodlands in the West are being permanently replaced by tracts of spiky shrubs. Conditions “just aren’t normal anymore,” one researcher said.
item.dc:creator: Eric Niiler and Nic Coury

item.title: Mapping America’s Largest ‘Dead Zone’
item.description: In a decades-long crisis, marine life has suffered as oxygen periodically dwindles in waters along the Gulf Coast.

item.title: Trump Announces a New Policy for a ‘Golden Age of Space Transportation’
item.description: The policy aims to greatly increase the number of spacecraft launches and re-entries.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang
item.media:description: The Trump administration wants to increase to 1,000 the number of rocket launches and spacecraft re-entries from space per year.

item.title: England’s Ancient Trees Are Dying in the Heat

item.dc:creator: Claire Moses
item.media:credit: Royal Society for the Protection of Birds, via Associated Press
item.media:description: The Major Oak at Sherwood Forest Nature Reserve in Nottinghamshire, England, in May.

item.title: This Skeleton is the First Confirmed Death by Trebuchet
item.description: Researchers believe a young man buried inside a Scottish castle was a victim of the long-feared siege weapon, more powerful than a typical catapult.
item.dc:creator: K. R. Callaway

item.title: NASA’s Attempt to Save the Swift Telescope Has Failed
item.description: NASA’s Swift Observatory, which studies some of the most powerful explosions in the universe, will soon burn up in the atmosphere.
item.dc:creator: Kenneth Chang

item.title: Humans Love Having Pets. Seems Like Some Other Primates Do, Too.
item.description: We aren’t the only animals that like to take care of other species. A new study finds that the roots of keeping a pet may stretch deep into our primate past.
item.dc:creator: Taylor Mitchell Brown

item.title: Nevada Sues Trump Administration Over Colorado River Cuts

item.title: The Ruthless Efficiency of Ultrapotent Street Drugs
item.description: Five decades after the “war on drugs” sought to make substance abuse unaffordable, illicit drugs are cheaper and more powerful than ever. A visit to Baltimore shows why.
item.dc:creator: Matt Richtel
item.media:credit: KT Kanazawich for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last summer, the city of Baltimore experienced several mass overdose crises, the result of fentanyl being mixed with powerful synthetic chemicals.

item.title: Trump Shuns E.V.s and Wind Power, But He’s Pouring Billions Into Batteries

item.dc:creator: Brad Plumer
item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Brandon Thibodeaux for The New York Times
item.media:description: While the Trump administration has rolled back efforts to expand clean energy, officials have come to see batteries as essential for many of their priorities.

item.title: Why Getting High Has Only Gotten Cheaper
